title: An $L^q$ bound from bounded pairings
statement: Let $(\alpha,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $q>1$, and let $u:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be integrable. Suppose $C\ge0$ and, for every essentially bounded measurable $g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$, the absolute value of $\int u g\,d\mu$ is at most $C$ times the $L^{q/(q-1)}(\mu)$ norm of $g$. Let $v:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable, nonnegative almost everywhere, and satisfy $v\le |u|$ almost everywhere; suppose also that $v\le B$ almost everywhere for some real number $B$. Then the $L^q(\mu)$ norm of $v$ is at most $C$.
